title: check-url waits on outbound feed parsing without a bounded timeout at the route boundary

evidence.quote:
processor = ContentProcessor()
        entries = await processor.parse_feed(url, max_entries=5)

reasoning: The route performs an outbound feed fetch as part of request handling and awaits it directly. There is no timeout or cancellation boundary in the route, so a slow or stalled public feed can keep the request open and consume server resources until the underlying parser returns. The broad exception fallback only handles eventual failures; it does not bound latency.
reproduction: Point /api/feeds/check-url at a public HTTP endpoint that accepts the connection but delays the response indefinitely; the request remains pending instead of returning within the configured fetch timeout.
recommendation: Wrap the feed parse call with a timeout, preferably the existing fetch timeout setting, and handle asyncio.TimeoutError explicitly. If parse_feed is intended to own timeouts, enforce it there and keep this route's behavior covered by tests.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not call POST /check-url and do not simulate slow feed parsing or timeout behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Monkeypatch ContentProcessor.parse_feed to await longer than the configured timeout, call POST /check-url, and assert the response completes with the intended fallback or error status within the timeout budget.
minimumFixScope: Add timeout handling around the parse_feed call used by check_feed_url and cover it in tests.
